newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Ceara to sell stake in Coelce.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Ceara to sell stake in Coelce.

text.p: The northeastern Brazilian state of Ceara plans to auction a 15 percent stake in its power distributor Coelce, the company's president said.
"We are planning to sell Coelce's 22.2 billion preferred shares, which account for 15 percent of its total stock," Coelce chief Jurandir Picanco told Reuters.
The stake equals 41 percent of all Coelce preferred or non-voting shares, he said.
Currently, Ceara state holds 89.5 percent of Coelce's voting or common stock and 71.4 percent of the firm's total capital.

Coelce, the third largest state-owned power utility in northeastern Brazil, has 1.3 million clients. Its sales last year totalled 475 million reais ($447.8 million), an increase of 8.9 percent over 1995.
Picanco said this would be the first step towards the privatization of the company, which is expected to occur in 1998's first quarter.
